payload.title: Getting Married in Italy as an Australian
payload.excerpt: Getting married in Italy as an Australian takes two documents, two countries and a sequence that has to run in the right order. Most guides online are written for British or American couples and talk about a Certificate of No Impediment, which Italy will not accept from you.
key_takeaways: Australians need two documents to marry in Italy: an Atto Notorio from the Italian consulate for your state, and a Nulla Osta sworn in person at the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Consulate-General in Milan.
Order certificates and apostilles early, because DFAT publishes no set turnaround and the Atto Notorio, signed with four unrelated witnesses, cannot be issued more than six months before the wedding.
In Italy the order is fixed: sign the Nulla Osta, legalise it at a Prefettura, then lodge your declaration at the comune before the ceremony.
An Italian marriage cannot be registered in Australia but is generally recognised here, so bring home the marriage certificate with an Apostille.

faq.q: Can Australians get legally married in Italy?
faq.a: Yes, with an Atto Notorio and a Nulla Osta, in a civil ceremony at the comune or a Catholic ceremony with civil effect. You cannot marry at the Australian Embassy.

faq.q: Am I legally married in Australia if I married overseas?
faq.a: In most cases, yes, if the marriage was valid where it took place and would have been valid in Australia.

faq.q: Do we need to register our Italian marriage in Australia?
faq.a: No. Overseas marriages cannot be registered here; keep the Italian certificate as evidence.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a Nulla Osta in Italy?
faq.a: It is signed at your appointment in Rome or Milan, then legalised at a Prefettura. Appointment lead times are not published, so book before you fly.

faq.q: How long is a Nulla Osta valid for?
faq.a: Six months, the same as the Atto Notorio.

faq.q: Can we use an Australian Certificate of No Impediment in Italy?
faq.a: No. The Embassy says Certificates of No Impediment are not valid for use in Italy.

faq.q: How early should we arrive in Italy before the wedding?
faq.a: It depends on the comune: the Embassy says the declaration and ceremony may fall on the same day, but some comuni want the declaration three days before. Add time for Rome or Milan and the Prefettura.

faq.q: Can we marry legally in Australia and have a symbolic ceremony in Italy?
faq.a: Yes. Lodge a Notice of Intended Marriage with an authorised celebrant at least one month before the Australian ceremony.
